fieldValues.title: Conformance Rules (RFC-049): the registry document
fieldValues.content: **[R9]** *(`ext:registry`)* The registry's held form and its travelling form are one JSON document, written by RFC-003 [C5]'s rules: UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, every object's members in ascending order of member name by Unicode code point at every depth, no duplicate names, array order kept except `entries`. `entries` MUST be ordered by `kind`; within a kind the writer supports, by the kind's identity fields in the order [R4] lists them, an absent field first; and every remaining tie and every entry of a kind the writer does not support by the entry's own [C5] serialization. All comparisons are of the text as written, by Unicode code point. The same build of a writer MUST write byte-identical files for identical content. A writer MUST stamp `registryRevision`, an integer that counts registry shapes only, with the revision of the shape it writes; this RFC's shape is `registryRevision` 1. A writer that rewrites a registry MUST keep entries, entry fields and top-level properties it does not understand, unchanged. A reader MUST read an absent stamp as revision 0, MUST refuse, loading nothing, a registry stamped above its supported revision, and MUST bring a registry stamped below it forward through a registry-form transformer for each intervening step, refusing it when a step has none. The step from 0 to 1 has this transformer: on every entry without `kind`, add `kind: "package"`, and replace `downloadUrl` by `locator: {mode: "remote", url: <downloadUrl>}` (an entry without `downloadUrl` gets no locator and fails as `entry-malformed`). How a registry is supplied (flag, file, environment) is the implementation's.
